title: The Crab That Won't Stay One
story: In the glass caverns beneath the salt flats, Mr 6 meets Octavene, a crackling crab the size of a shield. Every time a sword taps her shell, each crab present splits into 5 crabs — and the swarm's glow melts the cavern ceiling. Mr 6 sheathes his sword and counts instead: there is 1 crab now, and a careless hero would strike 4 times before realizing the problem.
question: If Mr 6 struck 4 times, how many crabs would be skittering around the cavern?
solution: Each strike multiplies the whole swarm by 5: after one strike 1 x 5 = 5 crabs.
Four strikes means 5 x 5 x 5 x 5 = 625 crabs.
A careless hero would face 625 crabs — Mr 6 thought first instead.
praise: Multiplying by 5 each round was the right idea — one more strike needed counting before you stopped.
hint: Write the swarm size after each strike: 1, then 5, then... keep going until you've struck four times.
victory: Mr 6 left his sword in its sheath, offered Octavene a cool tide-pool to live in, and she clacked away — still exactly one crab. Best battle he ever won by doing nothing at all.
imagePrompt: A glowing blue sparkcrab bristling with electricity in a cavern of glass salt pillars, a small numeral-six knight thoughtfully holding his sheathed sword and counting on his fingers in crackling violet light.
